description:
FOUND s501b (Opus, 2026-09-30) while fixing #2082 -- PRE-EXISTING on main 558cc5a0 (probed on the base extraction too), present since the initial import.  SILENT WRONG.

REPRODUCER (scratch/s501b/p/sys1.pl in the s501b worktree):
    system("cat"); system("cat", "-"); print "rc=$?\n";
`echo hi | perl sys1.pl` prints `hi` / `rc=0`; PCL prints only `rc=0`.

CAUSE: `%p-system-run` spawns with `:input nil` (SBCL: /dev/null), so the child never sees the program's STDIN.  perl's system is fork+exec: the child inherits descriptors 0/1/2.  `p-backtick` has the same `:input nil` AND `:error nil` -- a qx// child's STDERR is thrown away (perl: `my $x = qx(ls /nope)` prints the ls error on the terminal).  p-exec (s501b) already inherits all three (`:input t :output t :error t`).

CHEAP DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT: switch `:input nil` -> `:input t` in %p-system-run and run the probe; then `echo hi | ./runpcl` on `my $x = qx(cat); print $x`.  Risk to check: a program whose own STDIN is buffered by the Lisp reader (perl has the same buffering hazard, so matching perl is still the rule); the sweep runs perl-tests with STDIN from /dev/null, so no row should move -- measure it.

BAR: cl/ => full sweep + companion io/ + op/exec.t; guard rows in Pl/t/system-block-01.t.

=== s543c (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-21, CODE 64353611) ===
VERDICT: LIVE -- as filed (stdin = a file holding "hi"):
    system("cat"); print "rc=$?\n";        perl: hi / rc=0      PCL: rc=0
    my $x = qx(cat);                       perl qx=[hi]         PCL qx=[]
    qx(sh -c 'echo to-stderr 1>&2; echo out')  perl: "to-stderr" on the program's stderr, PCL: nothing on stderr (stdout part right)
LABEL: silent (subject now says so).

=== DONE (s543e, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-21) ===
MEASURED: %p-system-run spawned with `:input nil` (both arms), p-backtick with `:input nil :error nil` -- /dev/null for the child's stdin, the qx child's stderr discarded.  The piped opens (`-|`, `|-`) and exec already inherited (= perl).  A re-opened STDIN / STDERR is dup2'd onto 0 / 2 by %p-rebind-std, so inheriting the DESCRIPTOR is perl's semantics.
FIX (cl/): system `:input t`; qx `:input t :error t`; %p-stdin-give-back in %p-flush-all-output (a SEEKABLE STDIN is moved to its logical position before every child and at exit -- perl's PerlIOBuf_flush, so `<STDIN>; system("cat")` with a file stdin hands the child the rest, and `(prog; cat) < file` continues after what prog read); %p-child-stdio (a CLOSED STDOUT / STDERR is passed as the descriptor itself: `close STDERR; system(...)` answered -1 and never ran the command).
PROBES: scratch/s543e/p2/drive.pl (18 modes x file / pipe stdin = 36 runs): 34 = perl; the 2 others are an in-memory STDIN, where perl's own `open STDIN, '<', \$s` FAILS (docs/not-supported.md "An IN-MEMORY handle opened onto STDOUT/STDERR/STDIN").  multi.pl / rd.pl / gc.pl (read-ahead after readline / read / getc) = perl; `yes | prog` with a child that does not read: no hang (= perl); a closed stdin = perl.  NOT deterministic: the read-ahead from a PIPE stdin is lost to the child in both (how much depends on what the pipe held).
GUARD: Pl/t/system-block-01.t rows 48-50 (each feeds its own stdin file, never the gate's), inverse FAILS 48-50 on the base.  ir-spec §7.5b, DECIDED ## s543e.


=== CLOSED at MAIN-READY-104 `8959afae` (the reviewing session, 2026-11-21; s543e): a `system` child inherits descriptors 0 1 2, a `qx` child 0 and 2; guard Pl/t/system-block-01.t.  The batch`s 36 runs (34 = perl; 2 use an in-memory STDIN perl itself refuses) and the companion one-file runs op/exec.t io/pipe.t run/switches.t unchanged.  Not re-probed by the review beyond the gate (its rows feed their own stdin).
subject: SILENT WRONG: system() and qx// do not inherit the program's STDIN (and qx// discards the child's STDERR): `echo hi | prog` with `system("cat")` prints nothing, perl prints hi
triage_reason: system() / qx// do not inherit STDIN
